records.title: 2.7T Ignition Coil Pack Failure Causing Misfires and Flashing Check Engine Light
records.description: The 2.7T V6 used in A6 2.7T models is well known for ignition coil pack failures that cause sudden misfires, rough running, and loss of power. This issue was widespread across many early-2000s Audi/VW turbo models and generated numerous owner complaints and service actions. Failures may occur one cylinder at a time or in repeated succession as the coils age.
records.solution: Scan for cylinder-specific misfire faults, inspect spark plugs, and swap suspect coils to confirm the fault follows the coil. The standard repair is replacement of the failed coil packs; many owners replace the full set and install updated revision coils. Spark plugs should be checked or replaced at the same time if worn or fuel-fouled.

citations.title: Audi TSB 2023120/2: diagnose misfires and replace a coil only when the fault follows it

communityRecommendations.content: Label the coils before swapping them and rescan after the swap. A misfire that stays on the original cylinder points away from the coil.
Do not use recall 04V-133 as coil evidence; it is the A6 headlight-switch wiring and fire-risk recall.

records.title: Thermostat Housing Leak and Coolant Loss
records.description: The 2.0T thermostat housing in the 8R Q5 is made of plastic and develops cracks and seal failures due to thermal cycling. Located at the front of the engine, the housing leaks coolant that can drip onto the serpentine belt and accessory drive. The leak starts small and gradually worsens, typically appearing between 60,000 and 100,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the thermostat housing assembly with updated part. Consider an aluminum aftermarket housing for better durability. Replace the water pump and thermostat at the same time since they share access points and have similar failure intervals. Use G13 coolant specification for refill.
symptoms: Coolant leak from front of engine
Small coolant puddle under front of vehicle

records.title: 1990-1991 Audi 100 3-Speed Automatic Transaxle Recall 93V006
records.description: NHTSA campaign 93V006 covers 1990-1991 Audi 100 passenger cars equipped with a 3-speed automatic transmission. The campaign states that differential oil could be lost over time through evaporation, causing premature bearing and gear wear. Eventual differential failure could remove drive to the wheels or, in an extreme case, lock the front wheels and cause rapid deceleration. This is not a generic harsh-shift, solenoid or OBD-II DTC diagnosis.
records.solution: Check the VIN and campaign history with Audi or NHTSA. The historical campaign remedy drained the differential gear oil and replaced it with oil having higher-performance characteristics. Because these vehicles are more than 15 years old, confirm current remedy availability and any cost with Audi before service. Diagnose a present shift complaint separately and do not order a solenoid or filter kit from this card.
symptoms: Loss of drive if the differential fails
Possible front-wheel lock in an extreme differential failure

records.title: Hydraulic Assist System Leak (Pentosin)
records.description: The Audi 100 uses a complex mineral oil hydraulic system (Pentosin) that powers steering, brakes, and self-leveling suspension. Hoses, pump seals, and rack seals develop leaks, causing loss of power assist to steering and brakes simultaneously.

records.title: Power Steering Rack Seal Leak
records.description: The hydraulic power steering rack develops leaks from the input shaft seal and inner tie rod boots. Pentosin hydraulic fluid weeps and eventually pours from the rack, causing heavy steering and low fluid warnings.
records.solution: Replace or rebuild power steering rack. Use Pentosin CHF 11S fluid only — conventional ATF will destroy seals. Flush entire system when replacing rack. Check pump for whining which indicates damage from running low.

records.title: Timing Belt Failure on Interference V6 Causes Catastrophic Engine Damage
records.description: The Audi 100 V6 (AAH 2.8) is an interference engine: if the timing belt breaks or jumps, valves collide with pistons, resulting in bent valves and possible head/piston damage. Owners frequently neglect this on these older, lower-value cars, and the belt, tensioner, and idlers (plus the water pump driven by the belt) age out. Because of the engine's age, rubber components and the tensioner are well past their service life on most surviving cars. A snapped belt typically writes off the engine economically.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt on the manufacturer interval (roughly every 60,000-90,000 miles, or by age on these old cars) and always replace the tensioner, idler/roller, and the water pump at the same time. Use the correct cam/crank locking tools to set timing precisely, as slight misalignment on this interference engine causes valve-to-piston contact. If a belt has already failed, a compression/leak-down test and valve inspection are required before deciding on repair vs. engine replacement.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start (belt snapped)
Sudden loss of power while driving
Rattle or chirp from front timing cover area

records.title: 2009-2021 A4 2.0T Gasoline-Quality Deposit Diagnosis - TSB 2014753/13
records.description: Audi states that contaminated gasoline or gasoline with insufficient deposit-control additives can contribute to deposits on intake valves, the intake manifold, fuel injectors and combustion chambers. Possible results include rough running after cold start, extended cranking, hesitation, rough idle, reduced performance, poor fuel economy or an MIL with supported misfire, lean-system or cylinder-imbalance faults. This does not establish a universal A4 2.0T intake-valve defect, mandatory walnut-blasting interval or fixed failure mileage.

If contaminated gasoline is suspected, change fuel source; if detergent quality is suspect, Audi recommends Top Tier detergent gasoline. Identify the actual deposit location before selecting a cleaning process. Do not prescribe routine walnut blasting, a catch can, chemical cleaner or high-RPM driving from this record.

records.title: Engine Oil Leaks from Rear Cam Seal O-Ring and Valve Cover Gasket (I5)
records.description: The inline-five 80/90 commonly develops oil leaks at the back of the cylinder head. The rear cam seal is essentially an O-ring on the silver dust cap at the rear of the camshaft; it hardens and cracks with age and weeps oil. Combined with an aged valve cover gasket, oil seeps down the back and sides of the engine, where it can mimic a rear main seal or oil pan leak and make diagnosis confusing. These are age-related rubber seal failures typical of 30-year-old engines and are a frequent source of the oily film and burning smell owners report.
records.solution: Replace the rear cam seal/dust-cap O-ring together with the valve cover gasket; owners report a bone-dry engine afterward. Clean the area first to correctly locate the source, since valve-cover oil migrates and can be mistaken for lower-engine leaks. Use correct Audi/VW seals and torque the valve cover evenly.
symptoms: Oil film down back/side of engine
Apparent rear-main/oil-pan leak that is actually higher up

records.title: Hydraulic Brake Pressure Accumulator ("Bomb") Nitrogen Loss and Loss of Brake Assist
records.description: The Audi 90 quattro uses a central Pentosin hydraulic system that powers both the power steering and the brake servo. A nitrogen-charged pressure accumulator (universally nicknamed the "bomb") stores energy to provide brake boost if the pump or engine quits. The nitrogen gradually diffuses through the internal diaphragm, so almost all accumulators degrade after roughly seven years of service. As the charge bleeds down, the brake warning light stays lit for several seconds after start-up and, with the engine off, the pedal loses its power assist after fewer than about ten pumps. A weak or failed bomb makes the brake pedal hard and unboosted, sharply increasing stopping distances. The shared hydraulic pump and servo can also leak, and using ATF instead of Pentosin ruins the seals and sticks the accumulator check valves.
records.solution: Test the bomb by counting assisted pedal strokes with the engine off (loss of assist in under ~10 strokes indicates a depleted accumulator). Replace the pressure accumulator (P/N 893 612 061 C for pre-10/89 or 4A0 612 061 D for 1990-91), renewing the copper sealing washers/O-rings, and perform a complete Pentosin (CHF 11S) flush and refill with about 1 liter. If the fluid is old or dirty, a full bleed/refill may free a stuck valve before replacement is needed. Never substitute ATF. Inspect the hydraulic pump and servo return line for leaks at the same time.
symptoms: Brake warning light stays on several seconds after starting
Loss of brake boost after a few pedal pumps with engine off
Power steering and brakes feel heavy together

records.title: Hydraulic Valve Lifter Noise
records.description: The Audi 90 with the 2.3L and 2.8L engines develops noisy hydraulic valve lifters, especially on cold starts. The lifters bleed down overnight and tick until oil pressure builds up. Worn lifters may tick continuously.

records.title: Hydraulic Valve Lifter Tick on Cold Start
records.description: The 2.8L V6 hydraulic valve lifters (hydraulic lash adjusters) bleed down overnight, causing a ticking noise on cold start that lasts 30 seconds to several minutes. Worsens with age and infrequent oil changes.
records.solution: Try switching to high-quality full synthetic 5W-40 oil with fresh filter. If tick persists beyond 30 seconds, replace hydraulic lifters. Using VW 502.00 spec oil is recommended. Short oil change intervals (5,000 miles) help prevent recurrence.

records.title: Speedometer / Odometer Plastic Gear Failure (B4 Triggers Check Engine Light)
records.description: The VDO instrument cluster in the 80/90 uses small plastic gears in the speedometer/odometer assembly that strip teeth or break with age, a well-documented failure across the B3 and B4 chassis. The speedometer needle and odometer typically quit together. Crucially, on B4 cars the speed signal also feeds the engine ECU, so when the gear fails the ECU loses its vehicle-speed-sensor (VSS) signal and illuminates the MIL/check-engine light along with the dead speedometer. The original pot-metal/plastic gears are the weak point.
records.solution: Replace the failed speedometer/odometer gears with an aftermarket repair kit; Delrin replacement gears outlast the originals. The trip-odometer reset linkage can also break, so handle it carefully. On B4 cars, confirm the dead speedometer is the cause of the MIL before chasing other VSS faults. Repair is typically a cluster-out bench job.
symptoms: Check engine light / MIL on B4 models
Whirring or clicking noise from cluster

records.title: Timing Belt Failure Causing Bent Valves (Interference Engines NG/7A I5 and AAH V6)
records.description: All Audi 90 engines of this era - the NG and 7A 2.3L inline-fives and the AAH 2.8L V6 - are interference designs. If the rubber timing belt snaps, stretches, or jumps teeth, the pistons strike the open valves and bend them, turning a routine service item into a major engine repair. The belt, tensioner, and water pump are wear items; the belt can crack or stretch with age and the tensioner pulley weakens over time, allowing incorrect cam timing, misfires, or sudden engine stoppage. Owners are repeatedly warned that the AAH 12-valve V6 in particular is an interference engine where a broken belt means bent valves. Because these cars are now 30+ years old, belts often fail from age rather than mileage.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt, tensioner(s), and water pump together as a set on the manufacturer interval (roughly every 60,000 miles) or every 5-7 years regardless of mileage. Inspect the old belt for cracks/glazing and verify cam-to-crank timing marks on reassembly. On the V6 confirm correct tensioner setup, as incorrect timing causes immediate stoppage. Document the last belt service when buying one of these cars; if unknown, treat replacement as immediate maintenance.
symptoms: No-start with low compression after belt break

records.title: Water Intrusion into Footwells from Windshield Base and Sunroof Drains Damaging Electronics
records.description: B4-generation Audi 90/80 cars are notorious for water leaking into the front floor pans. Owners report water entering around the lower corners of the windshield and pooling in both front footwells, with the same pattern seen on nearly every junkyard B4. A second path is the sunroof drain system: the drain channels are poorly designed where the tubes connect, and the channel holes on both sides clog, causing water to overflow into the cabin. Water-soaked carpet and headliner create condensation and can short-circuit sensitive electronics (including modules near the ECU cover, where trapped debris blocks drainage). Left unaddressed it leads to corrosion and electrical faults.
records.solution: Clear and flush the sunroof drain channels and tubes; verify they exit freely. Inspect and reseal the windshield base/lower corners (a recently fitted windscreen can also be the culprit) and the ECU cover area, removing leaf debris so water drains. Dry out and treat any soaked carpet/insulation to prevent corrosion and electrical shorts.
symptoms: Intermittent electrical faults from water-damaged modules

records.title: Window Regulator Clip and Cable Failure
records.description: The plastic clips that attach the window glass to the regulator break, causing the window to drop into the door. The cable-driven regulator mechanism also frays over time. Very common failure on all four doors.
records.solution: Replace window regulator assembly. Aftermarket regulators with metal clips are more durable than OEM plastic clips. Lubricate window channels with silicone spray during installation.

records.title: 1.2 / 1.4 TFSI (EA111) Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
records.description: Early Audi A1 8X petrol cars fitted with the EA111 1.2 TFSI (CBZA/CBZB) and 1.4 TFSI (CAXA/CTHE/CAVG) engines suffer from a weak timing chain tensioner that loses hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to go slack and stretch. Combined with worn plastic chain guides, the camshaft timing drifts out of correlation with the crankshaft. If the chain jumps a tooth (commonly on cold start before oil pressure builds) the pistons can strike the valves, destroying the engine. The chain is at the back of the engine (gearbox side), making it labour-intensive to replace.
records.solution: Replace the full timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, and guide rails) with the uprated/superseded VAG parts, set timing with the correct locking tools, and reset adaptations. Keeping to short (max 10,000 km / ~6,000 mile) oil-change intervals with the correct VW 504/507 oil slows the wear. Listen for a rattle/whine on cold start as the early warning sign.
symptoms: Metallic rattle or whine on cold start

citations.title: CCPC / Audi Ireland - 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall

records.title: 1.4 TFSI Turbocharger Failure
records.description: The turbocharger on the 1.4 TFSI petrol A1 is a recognised weak point. The turbine/centre housing and bearings can fail, often aggravated by the engine's oil-consumption tendencies (oil starvation/coking of the turbo bearing). When it fails it produces a notable loss of power and smoke from the exhaust.
records.solution: Replace the turbocharger and address any underlying oil-feed/oil-consumption issue at the same time. Use the correct grade oil and let the engine idle briefly before shutdown after hard driving to protect turbo bearings.
symptoms: Black or blue smoke from exhaust
Whistling or whining from engine bay

records.title: 1.6 / 2.0 TDI Diesel DPF Clogging and EGR Valve Faults
records.description: The A1 is sold mainly as a town/city car, so diesel (1.6 TDI / 2.0 TDI) owners doing short, stop-start journeys never get the diesel particulate filter hot enough for passive regeneration. The DPF clogs with soot, and a faulty/sticking EGR valve accelerates this by raising soot output. Failed active regens can also dilute the engine oil with diesel. A blocked DPF triggers limp mode and is expensive to replace.
records.solution: Take the car on a sustained motorway run (~2,000+ rpm for 15-20 minutes) to force regeneration when the warning first appears. Clean or replace a faulty EGR valve, use the correct low-ash (504/507) oil, and forced/professional DPF cleaning if heavily blocked; replace the DPF if soot load is beyond recovery. Check oil level isn't rising from fuel dilution.

citations.title: CCPC / Audi Ireland - 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall

records.title: 7-Speed S tronic (DQ200 / 0AM) Dual-Clutch Mechatronic Failure
records.description: A1s fitted with the 7-speed dry-clutch S tronic (DQ200, VAG code 0AM) automatic suffer mechatronic (valve body / hydraulic control unit) failures. A design flaw in the valve body's accumulator/canister wall can crack and lose high hydraulic pressure, while the dry clutch packs wear and cause juddering. This led to a VAG recall covering A1s built roughly 2011-2016 (part of a wider ~80,000-vehicle UK action). Failure can cause sudden, complete loss of drive.
records.solution: Recondition or replace the mechatronic unit with the superseded/uprated valve body, update the transmission control software, and inspect/replace the clutch pack if worn. Check the recall has been completed on any used purchase. Regular DSG service (fluid for wet-clutch variants) helps; the dry DQ200 valve body fix is the core remedy.
symptoms: Judder / harsh 1st-to-2nd shift at low speed
PRNDS / gearbox warning flashing on dash
Sudden loss of drive or no drive

citations.title: CCPC / Audi Ireland - 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall

records.title: EA211 Water Pump / Thermostat Housing Coolant Leak
records.description: Later A1s using the EA211 family (1.0 TFSI three-cylinder and revised 1.4 TFSI) have an integrated, belt-driven water pump with a plastic thermostat housing bolted to it (two thermostats — one for block, one for head). The plastic housing and seals become brittle and leak, and the assembly can also be attacked by oil from a leaking PCV. Coolant escapes through a weep hole or housing gasket, leading to low coolant and overheating risk.
records.solution: Replace the complete coolant pump/thermostat assembly (rather than just the pump) with the updated part, as the plastic housings warp during partial disassembly. Replace seals and pressure-test the system. Special tools are needed for the thermostats.
symptoms: Coolant level dropping / low coolant warning
Engine running hot or fluctuating temperature

records.title: 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall
records.description: Audi Ireland and Ireland’s Competition and Consumer Protection Commission identify certain Audi A1 vehicles manufactured between 18 July and 14 October 2016. A supplier production-process change left some airbag and seat-belt-tensioner igniters outside prescribed tolerances, so an airbag or belt tensioner may not work correctly in a collision. This source does not establish the former windows, lamps, rattles or sunroof-motor aggregation.
records.solution: Ask an authorized Audi dealer to check the VIN and campaign-completion history. Audi Ireland’s notice says affected owners are contacted and the necessary refit is free of charge. Do not infer campaign eligibility from model year alone; only the VIN and production record establish whether this specific restraint-system work applies.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption on 1.2 / 1.4 TFSI (EA111) Engines
records.description: The early EA111 TFSI engines in the A1 are known to consume oil at an abnormal rate — owners report figures around 0.5 to 1.0 litre per 1,000 km. The root cause is the piston ring design (particularly the oil-control/scraper rings) which allows oil past the pistons into the combustion chamber where it is burned. Over time it worsens and can score the cylinder bores. The twin-charged 1.4 (supercharged + turbo) variants are especially affected.
records.solution: Confirm consumption with a controlled oil-consumption test. In mild cases monitor and top up; in advanced cases the genuine repair is replacing the pistons and piston rings (and inspecting/honing the bores). Updated piston/ring sets were introduced by VAG. Keeping oil topped up and changed on time prevents bore scoring and catalytic-converter damage.
symptoms: Oil level dropping quickly between services
Low oil pressure / oil warning light
Blue smoke from exhaust under acceleration

citations.title: CCPC / Audi Ireland - 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall

records.title: TFSI Direct-Injection Carbon Build-Up on Intake Valves
records.description: Because the TFSI engines (1.2/1.4 EA111 and EA211) inject fuel directly into the cylinder, no fuel washes over the intake valves. Oil vapour from the crankcase ventilation bakes onto the hot valves and intake ports over time, restricting airflow and causing misfires, rough idle and cold-start stumble — typically appearing from around 60,000-100,000 km.
records.solution: Physically clean the intake valves and ports, usually by walnut-shell media blasting with the intake manifold removed. Catch-can installation and good-quality oil can slow re-accumulation.

citations.title: CCPC / Audi Ireland - 2016 Audi A1 Airbag and Belt-Tensioner Igniter Recall

records.title: DQ381/DQ250 S tronic Mechatronic or Internal Transmission Fault Causing No-Drive, Jerking, or Gearbox Warning
records.description: Multiple A3/S3 owners report sudden gearbox malfunction warnings, harsh shifting, loss of drive, or the transmission becoming stuck in gear. On MQB-based A3 models with dual-clutch gearboxes, failures are commonly traced to the mechatronic unit, internal speed sensors, clutch adaptation faults, or internal transmission hardware. Audi/NHTSA documentation also shows recalls on certain newer A3/S3 vehicles for transmission-related defects that can lead to loss of motive power.
records.solution: Scan the transmission control module for stored faults and verify fluid condition, adaptation values, and clutch/mechatronic data. Depending on findings, repairs range from software update and basic settings/adaptation to mechatronic replacement or complete gearbox replacement. If the vehicle falls under an open recall or service action, Audi dealer diagnosis is important before paying out of pocket.
symptoms: Vehicle will not move in D or R

citations.title: NHTSA 2020 Audi A3 Recall Inventory

records.title: Haldex AWD Pump/Filter Contamination Leading to Rear AWD Loss on Quattro Models
records.description: Quattro A3 and S3 models using the Haldex coupling can lose rear-wheel engagement when the pump screen clogs or the pump fails. Owners often notice front-wheel-drive behavior, traction control intervention, reduced launch performance, or AWD malfunction messages. The issue is well known on MQB AWD cars and is often linked to overdue Haldex service or contamination in the pump pickup screen.
records.solution: Scan the AWD control module, verify pump activation, and inspect/clean the Haldex pump screen and fluid condition. Many cases are resolved with Haldex fluid service and pump cleaning, while others require pump replacement if the motor has failed. After repair, perform module output tests and confirm rear torque transfer on a road test.
symptoms: Reduced traction in snow or rain

citations.title: NHTSA 2020 Audi A3 Recall Inventory

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Glass Cracking or Exploding and Sunroof Frame/Rattle Problems
records.description: Owners of A3 sedan and Sportback/e-tron variants equipped with the panoramic roof have reported spontaneous glass cracking, loud popping noises, water leaks, and persistent roof rattles. Some complaints describe the outer panel shattering without impact, creating a safety concern from falling glass and sudden driver distraction. Other cases involve frame alignment or seal issues that lead to wind noise and leaks.
records.solution: Inspect the roof glass for stress cracks, frame distortion, and evidence of impact versus spontaneous failure. Repairs typically involve replacing the glass panel and, if needed, adjusting or replacing frame/seal components. If rattles or leaks are present, drains should be checked and the roof cassette alignment verified before replacing trim pieces.

citations.title: NHTSA 2020 Audi A3 Recall Inventory

records.title: DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) Clogging
records.description: The DPF can become clogged, especially with city driving and short trips that don't allow for proper regeneration cycles. This is more common after the emissions fix was applied. A clogged DPF causes reduced power and warning lights. OEM DPF assembly part numbers: 1K0254706LX (earlier production) and 1K0254708GX (later production). Fits 2009-2014 Audi A3 TDI with CBEA/CJAA engines. DPF differential pressure sensor: available from KermaTDI for CJAA/CKRA engines.
records.solution: Allow DPF regeneration by driving at highway speeds (65+ MPH) for 15-20 minutes regularly. For forced regen via VCDS: go to adaptation, enter security code 12233, change channel 18 from 0 to 1 while maintaining highway speed. Monitor soot levels via VCDS (Particle Filter Carbon Mass). If severely clogged, professional DPF cleaning with Liqui Moly 20110 DPF Cleaning Fluid (used with 20112 DPF Cleaning Flush and 7945/7946 spray tools) can help. Note: cleaning removes soot only, not ash - ash accumulation requires DPF replacement. OEM replacement DPF often back-ordered for weeks.
symptoms: Check engine light with DPF codes

citations.title: US EPA - Volkswagen Clean Air Act Civil Settlement and Audi A3 2.0L TDI Scope

records.title: EGR Valve/Cooler Failure
records.description: The EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) valve and cooler can fail from carbon buildup, causing rough running, poor performance, and warning lights. OEM EGR valve: 03L131501K (Pierburg, supersedes 03L131501G). OEM EGR cooler: 03L131512AF (Genuine Audi). EGR cooler valve: 03L131501F. EGR pipe to cooler: 03G131547H. EGR cooler temperature sensor: 03L906529A. EGR vacuum solenoid (N239/N345): 1K0906283A. EGR to intake manifold O-ring seal: 03G131547C.
records.solution: Clean or replace EGR valve (03L131501K). Inspect EGR cooler (03L131512AF) for leaks - coolant loss can indicate internal cooler failure. Regular intake cleaning helps prevent carbon buildup. Use quality diesel fuel. The EGR cooler removal process is documented at myturbodiesel.com for CBEA/CJAA engines.

records.title: 2010-2015 Audi A3 2.0L TDI Emissions Modification
records.description: The U.S. EPA identifies 2010-2015 Audi A3 2.0L diesel vehicles among the Volkswagen Group vehicles equipped with software that reduced emissions-control effectiveness during normal driving. Audi campaign 23Y9 separately documents the approved two-phase hardware and software modification for eligible 2015 A3 2.0L TDI vehicles. Scope and modification steps differ by generation and VIN.
records.solution: Check the VIN and emissions-modification status with Audi. Do not assume a historical buyback, settlement payment or extended-emissions-warranty term remains available today; ask Audi to confirm the exact completed phases and any current coverage in writing. Diagnose present DPF, EGR, turbo, fuel or drivability symptoms separately rather than buying parts from this campaign summary.

records.title: Glow Plug Failure
records.description: Glow plugs can fail, making cold starting difficult, especially in cold weather. The CBEA/CJAA engines use 'smart' glow plugs with integrated cylinder pressure sensors. OEM glow plug: 03L905061F (superseded to 03L905061K, then 03L905061M, current: 03L905061L). 4 plugs per engine. Glow plug control module (J179): 03L907281 (superseded to 03L907281B). Failed glow plugs can break during removal, requiring special extraction.
records.solution: Test glow plugs with VCDS if cold start issues occur - each plug can be tested individually. Replace failed glow plugs carefully - they can seize in the head. Soak with penetrating oil before removal. Use anti-seize on new plugs. Glow plug connector wiring (04L971785C) often breaks during service and should be kept on hand. Replace glow plug control module (03L907281) if faulty.

records.title: 2010-2012 Audi A3 2.0L TDI Injector-Line Recall 11V490
records.description: NHTSA campaign 11V490 covers 2010-2012 Audi A3 vehicles equipped with the 2.0L TDI common-rail diesel engine. Under specific load and RPM conditions, injection pulses can resonate with injector line number 2, adding stress that may create small cracks and fuel leakage. Fuel near an ignition source can cause a fire. The campaign does not establish universal injector, wiring-harness or fuel-rail failure.
records.solution: Check the VIN and campaign-completion history with Audi or NHTSA. The historical remedy installed an improved number-2 injector line on certain vehicles and vibration dampers on all injector lines. Because these vehicles are more than 15 years old, confirm current remedy availability and any cost with Audi. If diesel odor or visible leakage is present, shut the engine off and arrange inspection without driving.
symptoms: Diesel fuel odor from the engine compartment
Visible fuel leakage at injector line number 2

records.title: Turbocharger Failure
records.description: The BorgWarner BV43 variable-geometry turbocharger (OEM part 03L253056, BorgWarner 53039880208) can fail due to oil starvation, bearing wear, or variable geometry vane sticking/seizing. The most common failure mode is the variable vanes sticking or seizing, causing overboost or underboost. Catastrophic failures (compressor shaft snapping) are less common but documented. Failures typically occur around 100,000-150,000 miles.
records.solution: Regular oil changes with VW 507.00 spec diesel oil are critical - the turbo depends on clean oil for bearing lubrication. Replace turbo if failed using OEM BorgWarner unit (03L253056). Always replace the turbo oil feed line (03L145771) and oil return line (03G145736F) with new gaskets (03L145757Q oil return gasket) when replacing the turbo. Let engine idle 30-60 seconds before shutdown to allow turbo to cool down.
symptoms: Check engine light with boost codes

The infotainment main unit may be damaged internally when the vehicle is shut off, leaving the rearview-camera display inoperative the next time the vehicle is started. records.solution: Check the VIN and recall-completion history with Audi or NHTSA. The recall remedy replaces the infotainment main unit free of charge for eligible vehicles. If the rearview image is unavailable, use direct observation and mirrors and avoid relying on the display until the campaign or a separate diagnosis is completed.

records.title: 2020/2022-2024 Audi A3 2.0 TFSI Coolant-Pump Leak Diagnosis
records.description: Audi TSB 2071515/1 covers 2020 and 2022-2024 A3 vehicles with a 2.0 TFSI engine when the owner reports coolant loss, a leak or a coolant warning and the workshop can assign fresh leakage to the coolant pump. Audi warns technicians to distinguish a true leak from insufficient bleeding after production or an earlier repair.
records.solution: Document the suspected leak, clean and dry all traces, fill the system to the correct level and reassess after driving a few miles. If no fresh coolant returns, continue observing without replacing parts. If a leak recurs, replace only the component causing the damage under the exact VIN, engine and part criteria. Outside applicable warranty, Audi states the bulletin is informational.
symptoms: Coolant loss or visible coolant leak

records.title: 12V Battery Drain and No-Start from Faulty Gateway/Telematics Sleep Behavior
records.description: Multiple late-model Audi/VW MQB-derivative vehicles, including B9.5 A4s, have owner reports of repeated low-voltage warnings, dead batteries after sitting, and intermittent no-start conditions. The pattern is commonly linked to control modules not entering sleep mode properly, telematics/connectivity functions waking the network, or a weak AGM battery that tests marginal but repeatedly discharges. Owners typically report the car needing jump-starts after short parking periods and warning messages about electrical system malfunction or battery charge.
records.solution: Diagnosis should begin with battery state-of-health testing, charging-system verification, and parasitic draw measurement after the vehicle is allowed to sleep. Dealers often update software for gateway/telematics modules, check for excessive quiescent current, and replace the 12V AGM battery if it fails load testing; battery registration/coding is required after replacement. If draw remains high, scan all modules for wake-up faults and inspect accessories such as dashcams or OBD devices.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start after sitting
Intermittent warning lights after low voltage

records.title: Rear Differential Output Seal Leak
records.description: The quattro all-wheel drive rear differential can develop oil leaks at the output shaft seals. The seals dry out and crack over time, particularly in hot or arid climates. Low differential fluid can lead to bearing and gear damage if not caught early. Typically appears after 50,000-70,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the rear differential output shaft seals. Service the differential fluid (75W-90 GL-5) at the same time. Inspect the differential vent tube for blockage, as a clogged vent builds internal pressure that pushes seals out.
symptoms: Oil drip spots under rear of vehicle
Whining noise from rear differential under load
Fluid residue on rear differential housing
Burning oil smell from rear of car
Low differential fluid level at service

records.title: Rear hatch lift struts weaken and fail to hold the tailgate open
records.description: Both rear hatch gas struts on the B5 A4 Avant lose pressure over time as the internal seals dry out. Cold weather accelerates the failure. The first sign is the hatch slowly drifting downward after being opened; the second is the hatch dropping suddenly under its own weight, which can hit a person loading cargo. By 100,000 miles or 15 years almost every original-equipment strut has weakened past the point of holding the lid up. Some owners also report the strut ball mounts on the body backing out, allowing the struts to detach completely.
records.solution: Replace both struts as a pair — never one at a time, since unmatched strut pressures stress the hinges. OEM Stabilus struts from Audi or aftermarket equivalents (StrongArm, Strut Master, Hayman) cost $20-40 per pair. The job is 10-15 minutes with a flat-head screwdriver to release the spring clips on each ball end. If the body ball mounts have backed out, remove them, apply blue Loctite to the threads, and torque to ~22 N·m.
symptoms: Rear hatch drifts down slowly after being opened
Hatch drops suddenly when released, won't stay up
Hatch rebounds without latching when closing
Loose strut ball mounts rattle when door is shut
Cold-weather failure more pronounced than summer

records.title: Window regulator plastic clips and cable pulley fail, window drops into door
records.description: The B5 platform uses a cable-operated window regulator with green plastic clips holding the glass to the cable car. The clips are the dedicated wear point — they crack from heat cycling and cable tension, releasing the glass which then drops into the door cavity. Less commonly, the upper pulley (also plastic) shatters when the cable jumps off, severing the cable. The issue affects all B5 A4 body styles (sedan and Avant wagon) and is well-documented across the 1996-2001 production run. Failure pattern: window rolls down fine but will not go up, or rolls up briefly then drops back down.
records.solution: Two repair paths. Path 1 (cheap, fast): replace just the broken green clips — eBay/aftermarket sets are $20-30, swap takes 30 min per door without removing the regulator. Path 2 (durable): full regulator assembly with stainless or ball-bearing pulleys ($80-150 per door from ECS Tuning, FCP Euro, IDParts). Removing the old regulator requires drilling out the pop rivets on the door shell, so a heavy-duty rivet gun and replacement stainless rivets are needed. Many owners on later B5 cars do the full regulator job because the second clip fails within a year of the first.
symptoms: Rear window won't roll up, motor still spins
Window rolls up briefly then drops back down
Glass falls into the door cavity with a thunk
Grinding or fluttering noise from inside the door when switch is pressed
Window sits crooked in the channel

records.title: Bosch 5.3 ABS Control Module Internal Failure
records.description:
The problem begins with three beeps, a solid yellow ABS light and a flashing red brake light. The warning may come on momentarily while driving and go away, but in most cases will become more prevalent as time goes on. It seems to be a common problem with Audi A4 and VW Passat B5 models. These models use the Bosch 5.3 ABS system.
 
Failed Bosch 5.3 control modules are extremely common in 2000-era Audis.
 Internal bond-wire/solder-joint failures inside the controller (ultrasonically bonded substrate connections degrading in the hot engine bay) break communication with wheel-speed sensors and disable ABS/EDL.
records.solution:
A typical fault is: Control Module Part Number 8E0 614 111 M, Component/Version: ABS/EDS 5.3 QUATTRO D31, Software Coding 0273004134, Fault Found: 65535 - Internal Control Module Memory Error 35-00.
 
Audi does not sell the control unit by itself — you must purchase the entire Control Module, Pump and Valve assembly, which cost approximately $1950 for an 8E0 614 111 M.
 The economical fix is to unbolt only the electronic controller (6 Torx screws) and send it to Module Master, XeMODeX, or cheapabs.com for ~$150-350 rebuild with no recoding needed.

records.title: Retractable Cargo Cover Latch and Spring Failure

records.solution: Replace broken latch clips (available individually from Audi parts). If the retract spring is broken, the entire cargo cover cassette must be replaced. Aftermarket covers are available at lower cost than OEM.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Tube Clogging
records.description: The panoramic sunroof drain tubes on the A4 Avant clog with debris, causing water to overflow into the headliner, A-pillars, and footwells. Left unchecked, this damages the electronics under the carpet including the comfort control module.
records.solution: Clear all four sunroof drain tubes using compressed air or a flexible cleaning wire. Clean the sunroof channel tray. Inspect and replace any cracked drain tube connections at the roof corners.

records.title: Rear Upper Shock Mount Bushing Wear
records.description: Rear upper shock mount bushings wear out, causing a knocking noise from the rear when going over bumps. The Avant's heavier rear end accelerates bushing wear compared to the sedan. Common after 60,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace rear upper shock mount bushings. Consider replacing rear shocks at the same time if over 80,000 miles. Bilstein B4 or Sachs OE replacements are recommended. Realign rear suspension after service.

records.title: 1.8T oil sludge clogs pickup tube and starves engine of oil
records.description:
Engine oil sludge is a well-documented issue on the longitudinally-mounted 1.8T in the B5 A4. 
Volkswagen of America warned 426,000 VW Passat and Audi A4 owners of an engine oil sludge problem affecting 1.8-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engines on 1998 to 2004 Passats and 1997 to 2004 A4s
, and 
Audi offered an 8 years unlimited mileage extended warranty for the oil sludge issue
 provided the owner could show proof of oil change intervals.

Sludge is the thickening/coking of engine oil due to heat and moisture. 
Turbocharged engines generate a lot of heat near the compressor turbine — the turbo shaft bearing is a mere ¼ inch away from 900° temperatures. When turbocharged engines are driven hard, oil within the turbo can heat up to a point where it begins to break down and forms solid particles, especially if an engine is shut down before the turbo can cool down. This cooked oil forms large particles which pass down into the sump and are then sucked into the pickup tube
. 
The longitudinally mounted 1.8t engines in the B5-B6 models had a smaller oil pan than their transverse mounted cousins, making the engine more susceptible to overheating and sludge
.


Over time, these particulates flake off and make their way down into the oil pan, eventually clogging the oil pick-up screen. This restriction limits the flow of oil to the point where the oil pump can no longer supply the necessary amount of pressurized oil to the system
, ultimately leading to turbocharger and bearing failure.
records.solution:
Audi's sludge service replaces the oil pump pickup, turbo oil feed line, crankcase vent pipes/PCV valve, reseals the oil pan, replaces the valve cover gasket, and replaces the cam tensioner if worn. 
Use synthetic oil that meets the VW 502 00 standard
 and change every 5,000 miles. Upgrade to the larger 068-115-561-B (or equivalent) oil filter, which holds more oil and catches more debris. For DIY, dropping the oil pan and cleaning the pickup screen costs ~$300 in parts; 
one owner had a trusted mechanic replace the oil pump pickup tube for $450 and the old tube came out plugged
; full sludge remediation at a shop runs $1,500-$3,500, and an engine replacement (which Audi sometimes performed under the TSB) is significantly more. 
If the pickup is already clogged, do not run engine flushes such as Seafoam — they may dislodge sludge buildup causing other problems such as plugging the turbo oil supply and killing the turbo
.
symptoms: oil pressure light flickers at idle or low rpm

records.title: Central locking vacuum pump fails: shattered graphite impeller or water-intrusion fried electronics
records.description:
The pneumatic central locking pump/module is located in the right-rear corner of the trunk under the trim. 
The heart of the system is the central locking pump control module (CLP) located in the trunk. It's in the right rear corner of the A4 & S4. The CLP consists of a graphite rotary-vane pump driven by an electric motor that generates air pressure or vacuum that locks and unlocks the doors, trunk, & fuel door.
 Two common failure modes: 
The Audi pneumatic central locking system is plagued by several common problems as it ages. The most common problem is when the internal graphite parts of the air pump wear out and shatter. This is the result of normal use and wear. Many people have observed the locks taking longer and longer to unlock over a period of weeks or months as the pump parts are in their final stages of life.
 Second mode is electronics failure from water intrusion: 
failure of the electronics due to water intrusion into the trunk. In extreme cases the electronics failure can cause the CLP to run until it heats up and melts. Water intrusion on the A4 & S4 models is often through a faulty trunk seal or faulty right side tail light seal.
 A third mode is a slow leak in the plastic tubing (most common at the driver's-door hinge) that causes the pump to over-run; sustained over-run is what eventually shatters the graphite impeller.
records.solution:
Open the trunk and pull back the right-side liner — if the foam block around the pump is wet, the right tail-light seal and/or trunk seal must be fixed before any new pump will survive. Test by listening: if the motor hums but produces no pressure/vacuum at the nipples, the internal graphite vanes have shattered. If the pump runs continuously until timeout, suspect a leak in the plastic vacuum lines (common at the door-T fittings), dried hose-connector O-rings, or the pump's internal pressure-cutoff diaphragm/contacts. 
The pump runs until it meets pressure, or times out — a common fix is a small split in one of the tubes over a nipple, which can be cut off and patched with a piece of rubber tubing.
 Used CLPs run $50-150, new ~$300-500; dealer replacement totals $500-700. Module part numbers 8D0862257B/N (pre-facelift) and 8L0862257B/N (facelift) for B5 A4 — board can be swapped to retain coding, or pump motor/graphite can be transplanted from a cheap VW Passat/Jetta donor unit.
symptoms: doors fail to lock/unlock from key or remote
burning smell from rear of trunk
locks taking progressively longer to actuate over weeks/months

records.title: Front upper/lower control arm bushing and ball-joint failure causes clunking
records.description:
One of the most common suspension issues seen on Audi A4s is worn or failed control arm bushings; the bushings receive the most pressure during braking or heavy acceleration, and these forces cause the rubber to fatigue and crack
. 
When inspecting at the inboard end where the control arm mounts to the chassis, you may see cracks, leaks or missing pieces of rubber, and at low speeds hear a clunking or creaking noise when traveling over a speed bump
. 
On the B5 A4, both upper and lower control arms wear — owners commonly report needing one upper on one side and a lower on the other
.
records.solution:
Raise the car using a jack, find the suspected control arm, move it manually to check for looseness, and have a friend bounce the car so you can listen for noises
. Most B5 owners replace the full set of 8 front control arms ('boomerang' kit) at the same time since labor overlaps. 
Replacing the control arms can be done for around $200-250 in parts if you do the work yourself
; a shop replacement typically runs $800–$1,400 for the full front-end refresh. Use OEM-quality brands (Lemförder, Meyle HD, TRW) — cheap eBay arms commonly fail within 20-30k miles.
symptoms: clunking or creaking over bumps and speed humps

records.title: G62 Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor (black-housing) fails causing erratic temp gauge, hard cold starts and rich-running
records.description:
The original black-housing dual coolant temperature sensor (G62) mounted in the coolant flange at the back of the cylinder head develops cracks and fails internally. 
The temperature sensor G2 (also known as G62) for the gauge has likely failed and is relatively easy to fix; it is located in the coolant flange at the back of the cylinder head and the early square-connector style and later elongated D-shaped black connector sensors are known problematic units.
 When it fails the ECU sees an implausible coolant temperature, leading to 
cold starting difficulties at low temperatures, poor idle and acceleration during warm up
 as well as an erratic or dead temperature gauge.
records.solution:
Scan with VAG-COM/VCDS for fault 17664 / 16502 (P0118) and bench-test the sensor's resistance. 
From Bentley, the G62 test procedure: allow engine to cool to room temp (68F/20C), disconnect ECT sensor, connect multimeter to terminals 1 and 2; resistance must be 1500 to 3000 ohms — if not, replace the ECT.
 Replace with the updated green-top OEM sensor (part 059 919 501A) along with the retaining clip (032 121 142) and O-ring; 
replacing this sensor resolves running issues for many owners who are still using the original black sensor which had a high failure rate.
 Part is ~$25-40, DIY 30 minutes; shop labor brings total to ~$80-180.
symptoms: erratic or dead coolant temperature gauge

records.title: Instrument cluster (MID) and climate control LCD pixel/segment failure
records.description:
The large red multi-function display in the center of the B5 instrument cluster (Jaeger/VDO speedometers) and the smaller climate control LCD both lose pixel rows and segments as the silver-conductive ribbon-to-LCD bond degrades with heat cycles. 
The common thing is the big red fading LCD in the middle, with missing lines or columns and disappearing LCD pixels (sometimes getting worse when warmed up).
 Drivers see missing lines/columns in the odometer, trip computer, gear selector indicator, and HVAC temperature readout — often worse when the cabin is warm. The fault is cosmetic-to-nuisance grade but can hide important warnings (oil temp, mileage).
records.solution:
For the instrument cluster, replace the LCD ribbon cable or full LCD module (Minitools SEPDISP09, Module Master, or Pixelfix kits, ~$30-80) — 
requires removing the two torx screws holding the cluster, pulling it out of the dash, and disconnecting the three connectors on the back (push purple retaining clips upwards)
, then disassembly and careful soldering of a ribbon connector. 
The SEPDISP09 consists of an LCD display with FPC to be soldered (using tin solder) to the main board of the dashboard, and a good level of skill and soldering experience are required.
 For the climate control LCD, a plug-and-play LCD kit (Module Master/Circuit Solutions ~$60) installs in roughly 30 minutes. 
Module Master will swap out the LCD for something like $150 and takes about a week
, so send-in repair services run roughly $100-200 if you prefer not to DIY.
symptoms: missing rows/columns on red MID display
blank or partial HVAC temperature digits
fading display when interior warms up

records.title: B6/B7 Front Suspension Control Arm and Tie-Rod Wear Causing Clunks, Vibration, and Uneven Tire Wear
records.description: The multi-link front suspension used on B6/B7 A4 models is well known for premature wear of upper and lower control arm bushings/ball joints and, in many cases, outer tie-rod ends. Owners commonly report front-end clunking over bumps, looseness in steering, shimmy at highway speeds, and abnormal inner-edge tire wear. The issue is widely documented in owner forums and repair databases because multiple arms can wear at once, making the front end feel unstable even when alignment is repeatedly corrected.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually involves checking each front control arm ball joint and bushing for play with the suspension loaded, along with inspecting tie rods and verifying alignment. The durable fix is replacing the worn arms as a matched kit rather than one-by-one, followed by a proper four-wheel alignment. If pinch bolts are seized, additional labor is often required, and sway bar links should be inspected at the same time.

records.title: 2002-2006 A4 Factory-CVT Settlement History - Component-Specific Diagnosis
records.description: The 2013 settlement covered U.S. 2002-2006 A4 vehicles originally equipped with a factory-installed CVT. It used component-specific branches: TCM for 2003-2006; valve body for 2003-2004; and transmission without valve body/TCM for 2002-2004, subject to maintenance proof. Plaintiffs alleged improper function, while defendants denied defect, wrongdoing and liability and the court did not decide the merits. The notice does not establish every CVT symptom as a failed transmission.
records.solution: Verify the VIN, original U.S. factory-CVT equipment, transmission code, faults, fluid/maintenance records and reproducible behavior. Diagnose the TCM, valve body and mechanical transmission separately and replace only the confirmed component. The historical 10-year/100,000-mile terms and November 18, 2013 reimbursement deadline are expired; do not promise coverage or buy a TCM, valve body or transmission from this record.
affectedSystems: transmission excluding valve body and TCM for 2002-2004

records.title: 2022-2025 A4 Brake Squeal or Pulsation Diagnosis - TSBs 2051095/8 and 2022584/12
records.description: Audi’s through-model-year-2025 brake bulletins distinguish squeal from pulsation. TSB 2051095/8 states that brake squeal alone does not indicate a defect and uses noise frequency and VIN-specific repair information. TSB 2022584/12 covers steering-wheel vibration or brake-pedal pulsation during braking and lists multiple possible causes rather than one rotor/pad defect. Neither bulletin supplies a DTC.
records.solution: Confirm whether the complaint is sound, steering-wheel vibration, pedal pulsation or an actual braking-performance concern. Check the VIN for the applicable current bulletin, reproduce and document the frequency/speed/temperature conditions, measure the brake system and diagnose tire, hub, rotor, pad and installation causes as directed. Replace only confirmed components; do not buy pads and rotors from this record.

rotor, pad, hub and installation interfaces

records.title: Instrument Cluster LCD Pixel Failure and Intermittent Gauge/Warning Display Problems
records.description: B5 and early B6 A4 models commonly suffer from failing instrument cluster displays, especially the center LCD where outside temperature, warning messages, and trip computer information become unreadable due to missing pixels. Some owners also report intermittent gauge behavior or fading displays that worsen with heat. This is a well-known age-related electronics issue documented across forums and complaint records because it affects visibility of warning information and often requires cluster repair or replacement.
records.solution: Confirm whether the problem is limited to the LCD ribbon/display or whether the cluster has broader internal faults. Specialist rebuilders can often repair the pixel display and restore the cluster without replacing the entire unit, while replacement clusters require immobilizer matching/coding on applicable years. Battery voltage and charging system health should also be checked because low voltage can aggravate display behavior.

records.title: Sunroof Drain/Seal Water Intrusion Causing Wet Carpets and Interior Electronics Concerns
records.description: Panoramic/sunroof-equipped A4s continue to generate owner complaints about water entering the cabin, usually from clogged drains, disconnected drain tubes, or seal alignment issues. Owners often first notice damp headliners, wet front or rear carpets, musty odors, or intermittent electrical warnings after heavy rain or car washes. If water reaches under-carpet wiring or modules, repair costs can rise quickly beyond a simple drain cleaning.
records.solution: Inspect all sunroof drains for blockage and verify that each drain tube is properly attached and flowing. Check the sunroof frame, cassette seals, and door vapor barriers if the leak source is unclear; then dry the interior thoroughly and inspect under-carpet connectors/modules for corrosion. Early intervention is important because mold and wiring damage can turn a minor leak into a major interior electrical repair.
symptoms: Water dripping from headliner or A-pillar area

records.title: Severe Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (Direct Injection)
records.description: All direct-injection engines in the A5 and S5 (2.0 TFSI, 3.0T, and 3.2L V6) suffer from severe carbon buildup on intake valves. In direct-injection engines, fuel sprays directly into the cylinder, bypassing the intake valves. This means intake valves are only exposed to oil vapors from the PCV system, which bake onto the valve backs as hard carbon deposits. Over 60,000-100,000 miles, carbon restricts airflow, causing rough idle, misfires, hesitation, and power loss. The 3.0T supercharged S5 is particularly susceptible due to higher oil vapor pressure. In severe cases, carbon deposits prevent valves from seating properly, causing compression loss and valve damage. The ONLY effective fix is walnut blasting—blasting crushed walnut shells through the intake to remove carbon. A5OC forums recommend this as preventive maintenance every 60,000 miles.
records.solution: WALNUT BLASTING: Remove intake manifold and blast crushed walnut shells through intake ports to remove carbon ($700-$1,200). Requires specialized equipment—DIY not recommended unless experienced. Dealers charge $1,200-$1,800; independent Audi shops charge less. Repeat every 60,000-80,000 miles as preventive maintenance. PREVENTION: Install catch can ($300-$500) to filter PCV oil vapors before they reach intake valves—extends cleaning interval to 100k+ miles. Add Liqui Moly Intake Valve Cleaner to every oil change ($15). Perform "Italian tune-up" monthly (spirited highway driving to high RPM).
symptoms: Rough or unstable idle (engine shakes at stoplights)
Reduced power and sluggish throttle response
Check engine light with misfire codes (P0300-P0306)
Engine runs rough when cold, smooths out when warm

records.title: S-Tronic/DSG Mechatronic Unit Failure
records.description: The 7-speed S-Tronic (DL501) dual-clutch transmission in the A5 suffers from mechatronic unit failures. The mechatronic unit is the electro-hydraulic control module that manages gear selection and clutch engagement. Internal solenoid and valve body wear causes erratic shifting, shuddering, and eventual loss of gears.
records.solution: Replace or rebuild the mechatronic unit. Audi dealers replace the entire unit ($3,000-$5,000), but specialized transmission shops can rebuild the existing unit for $1,500-$2,500. Regular fluid changes every 40,000 miles with correct Pentosin FFL-2 fluid can extend mechatronic life significantly.
symptoms: Harsh or jerky shifts between 1st and 2nd gear
Delayed engagement when shifting from P to D
Clunking noise when coming to a stop
Transmission stuck in neutral or limp mode
Gear selection flashing on instrument cluster

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption (2.0 TFSI Engine)
records.description: The 2.0 TFSI engine in early B8 A5 models (2008-2015) suffers from excessive oil consumption due to defective piston ring design. Owners report burning 1 quart of oil every 500-1,200 miles, requiring constant top-ups. The issue is worst in 2010-2012 models with EA888 Gen 2 engines. Faulty oil control rings fail to scrape oil from cylinder walls, allowing it to burn in the combustion chamber. This causes blue smoke on startup, fouled spark plugs, and carbon buildup. Low oil levels starve the turbocharger and timing chain tensioners, leading to expensive failures. Audi extended warranty coverage for some models and performed piston ring replacements under warranty. A5OC forums report many owners going through 5+ quarts between oil changes. Some cases cause cylinder scoring requiring engine replacement.
records.solution: For SEVERE consumption (over 1 qt/1,000 mi): Piston ring replacement or short block replacement ($4,000-$7,000). Check Audi's extended warranty program for 2009-2015 models—some repairs covered. For MODERATE consumption: Replace PCV valve ($150), clean carbon deposits with walnut blasting ($800), and switch to thicker oil (5W-40 instead of 5W-30). PREVENTION: Check oil level WEEKLY, change oil every 5,000 miles (NOT 10,000), and avoid 2010-2012 models when buying used. 2015+ Gen 3 EA888 engines have updated rings and are far more reliable.
symptoms: Low oil warning light frequently (need to add oil between changes)
Burning 1+ quarts of oil every 1,000 miles
Blue or gray smoke from exhaust on startup or hard acceleration
Check engine light with misfire codes (P0300-P0304)

records.title: 2018-2023 A5 Sportback Trunk-Strut Hydraulic or Chafing Noise
records.description: Audi TSB 2062669/2 covers hydraulic-flow or chafing sounds from the trunk-lid struts while opening or closing a 2018-2023 A5 Sportback. Audi describes these sounds as a normal, design-related strut characteristic whose frequency and intensity can vary with temperature and operating speed; the bulletin does not establish weak struts or a hatch that can fall.
records.solution: Compare the complaint with the hydraulic-flow or functional noise described by Audi while operating the trunk lid. Audi states that replacing parts does not solve this noise condition. A hatch that will not remain open, closes unexpectedly or has abnormal powered-lift operation is a different safety-relevant symptom and should be diagnosed independently rather than treated from this informational card.

records.title: EA888 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure
records.description: The A5 shares the B8/B8.5 platform with the A4 and inherits the same EA888 2.0T timing chain tensioner weakness. The original tensioner design allows the chain to slacken on cold starts, eventually jumping teeth and causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact. Pre-2013 engines are most affected.
records.solution: Replace timing chain, tensioner (use latest revision 06K109467K), and all guides as a complete kit. Preventive replacement recommended at 80,000-100,000 miles before symptoms appear. If chain has already jumped, engine teardown is required to assess valve and piston damage.

Check engine light with timing correlation codes
Metallic chain slap noise from front of engine

records.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure (2.0 TFSI Engine)
records.description: The B8/B8.5 A5 with the 2.0 TFSI engine (2008-2016) suffers from premature timing chain tensioner failure, identical to the A4 and A6. The tensioners wear out between 60,000-120,000 miles, causing the timing chain to stretch and rattle. A loud rattling noise on cold start from the front of the engine is the classic warning sign. If ignored, the timing chain can jump timing or break, causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact and destroying the engine. Early B8 models (2008-2012) are more prone to failure than later B8.5 models (2013-2016). A5OC forum members report many failures under 100,000 miles, with some owners experiencing complete engine destruction. The repair requires removing the front of the engine and costs $2,000-$5,000. Some owners report oil consumption issues leading to accelerated tensioner wear.
records.solution: PREVENTIVE REPLACEMENT: Replace timing chain, tensioners, and guides at 80,000-100,000 miles BEFORE rattling starts ($2,000-$3,000). If rattling has already begun, DO NOT delay—chain can jump at any moment. Repair requires removing front engine cover, water pump, and thermostat. Labor is 8-12 hours. Use ONLY OEM Audi parts—aftermarket tensioners fail quickly. Change oil every 5,000 miles and check oil level weekly to prevent accelerated wear. If catastrophic failure occurs, engine replacement ($6,000-$10,000) may be more cost-effective than rebuild.
symptoms: Loud rattling or clattering noise from front of engine on cold start
Metallic rattling that disappears after 10-30 seconds of warm-up
Check engine light with timing correlation codes (P0016, P0017, P0087)
Engine won't start (if chain has jumped)
Catastrophic engine damage if chain breaks (bent valves, destroyed pistons)

records.title: C5 A6 2.7T Low Boost or Smoke - Diagnose the System Before Buying a Turbo
records.description: The 2000-2002 C5 A6 Quattro 2.7T APB uses two position-specific turbochargers plus wastegate control, N75 regulation, recirculation valves, vacuum plumbing, charge-air hoses/intercoolers, crankcase ventilation, and separate oil/coolant connections. Low boost, noise, or exhaust smoke does not identify a turbocharger or a side by itself. Audi's diagnostic information specifically requires a leak-tight vacuum/charge system and notes that a recirculation valve or vacuum-line fault can produce no boost and rumbling. The previous card treated those symptoms as a predictable heat/oil failure across 2000-2004, added unsupported mileage and cost ranges, and sent every owner to a right-side 078145702R search before the failed component or bank was known.
records.solution: Save DTCs and freeze-frame, then compare commanded and measured boost using the factory test conditions. Pressure- or smoke-test the intake and charge-air path; inspect intercoolers, clamps, vacuum hoses, both recirculation valves, N75 control, wastegate operation, crankcase ventilation, and oil/coolant leakage. Determine whether smoke is entering through the intake, exhaust, or crankcase system. A turbo specialist should confirm wheel damage, housing contact, bearing/shaft condition, or a failed seal and identify bank/side before parts are ordered. If a turbocharger is mechanically confirmed failed, match the APB engine, VIN, transmission, left/right position, and current Audi/BorgWarner revision; follow the factory procedure for new seals/fasteners, oil and coolant connections, cleanliness, and pre-lubrication. Because neither the current symptom record nor ShowMeTheParts establishes a failed side, this card intentionally provides no turbo purchase link.
symptoms: Measured boost is below specification after test conditions are met
Blue or gray exhaust smoke whose source has not yet been isolated
Whine, rumble, or mechanical noise under boost
Oil present in charge plumbing beyond the level a technician considers normal
Loss of power or boost-control fault that may also be caused by leaks or control components

records.title: Timing belt/tensioner failure causes catastrophic valve-piston contact
records.description: The 2.8L V6 (both 12V AAH in the C4 1995-1997 and 30V AHA/ATQ in the C5 starting 1998) is an interference engine, so timing belt, tensioner, idler, or hydraulic damper failure between service intervals will allow the valves to strike the pistons, bending valves and sometimes cracking pistons. The hydraulic tensioner damper on the 30V is a well-known weak point — owners report aftermarket 'OEM-quality' dampers collapsing within about a week of installation, causing audible belt slap. Audi's most recent recommended belt-replacement interval is 75,000 miles (some older service booklets referenced 105,000 miles, and earlier model-year intervals were shorter).
records.solution: Replace the timing belt as a complete kit (belt, tensioner roller, tensioner lever, hydraulic damper, idler/relay roller, and water pump) at or before the service interval — do not just replace the belt. Use OEM or reputable brands (NTN for the hydraulic damper, INA for idler bearings, Continental/ContiTech for the belt); forum reports document cheap aftermarket dampers failing within days. The hydraulic damper must be compressed slowly to avoid irreversible internal damage. Camshaft alignment bar (Audi tool 3242) and crankshaft lock pin (Audi tool 3391) are required to set timing accurately on the 30V. Parts kit runs roughly $300-600; a full job at an independent shop typically runs $900-1,800. Catastrophic failure repair (valves, possible head work) commonly runs $2,500-4,500+.
symptoms: belt slap or slapping noise at idle
bent valves / no compression after failure

records.title: 48V Belt Starter-Generator Warning and VIN-Specific Campaigns
records.description: A 48V electrical-system warning on a mild-hybrid A6 is not repaired with an ordinary 12V battery, charger, alternator, or starter. Outside those campaigns, the exact Audi fault code and symptom number matter: U046900 with symptom 34763 and actual mode 8 can point to another CAN or sensor fault, and Audi states that replacing the starter generator will not fix that case.

For a warning outside an open campaign, use Audi ODIS-guided diagnosis and preserve the complete code, symptom number, and actual mode. U046900 or P0CA700 alone is not permission to order a starter generator. Audi must select the correct starter-alternator suffix and associated hardware by VIN and guided-test result. Do not buy any of the former Optima, ACDelco, Battery Tender, Denso, or Remy 12V products for this 48V fault.

records.title: 2012-2015 A6 ABS/ESP Warning With Engine Will Not Switch Off
records.description: Audi TSB 2037761/1 covers a specific situation in which a 2012-2015 A6 shows ABS/ESP warnings and the engine does not switch off with a normal press of START ENGINE STOP. The ignition system uses the ABS control unit's vehicle-speed signal to determine whether the car is stationary. A control-module/signal fault can remove that signal; prolonged wheel slip in winter can also make wheel speeds appear implausible and temporarily deactivate ABS even when there is no permanent system error. The previous record duplicated the older C5 Bosch-module card and sent users to a 4B0614517P search without establishing vehicle generation, DTC, system version, or a failed module.
records.solution: Bring the vehicle to a complete stop in a safe location. Audi states that below 6 mph (10 km/h), the emergency-off function is activated by holding START ENGINE STOP while pressing the brake pedal. Diagnose the vehicle according to the stored DTCs rather than ordering an ABS module from the warning alone. If the warning followed sustained winter wheel slip, Audi notes that the system may become fully active again after the ignition is switched off and the vehicle is restarted; persistent warnings still require diagnosis. Do not use the emergency-off procedure while driving except as described by the owner's manual and Audi safety information. This informational bulletin specifies no replacement part, so this record has no commerce link.

A normal press of START ENGINE STOP does not switch off the engine while stopped
The condition may follow loss of the ABS speed signal or prolonged winter wheel slip

records.title: 2018-2021 A6 Adaptive Suspension - Verify Compressor Pressure With a Physical Tester
records.description: Audi TSB 2062932/1 describes an informational diagnostic issue on 2018-2021 A6/A7 vehicles with adaptive suspension. During PDI or diagnosis, ODIS address 0074 may show accumulator or system pressure above 25 bar even though that is not the actual pressure; some J775 suspension-control-module versions report the measuring value incorrectly. The previous card instead claimed that 2012-2018 Premium Plus and Prestige A6 sedans commonly burn out compressors at a fixed mileage, assigned 1,400 owner reports without source evidence, and recommended Arnott P-3250, relay 8K0951253, and compressor 4G0616005C without proving the vehicle had adaptive air suspension or that any of those parts matched.
records.solution: First confirm by VIN/PR equipment that the vehicle has adaptive suspension. If ODIS address 0074 shows accumulator or system pressure above 25 bar, do not condemn the compressor from that value. Audi specifies using air-suspension leak-detection tester VAS 751 001 to measure actual pressure and evaluate compressor output. A real sag, leak, run-time, or ride-height complaint still requires the separate factory leak, valve-block, air-spring, relay, wiring, temperature-protection, and compressor diagnostics for that VIN. Replace a compressor only after measured output and the rest of the air-supply system identify it as failed. This bulletin itself specifies a diagnostic tool rather than a replacement part, so the old product links are removed.

records.description: Audi TSB 2067906/5 explains that the 48V battery can enter low-state-of-charge protection and open its internal relays. P0A7D00 can accompany this condition. records.title: C5 A6 Bosch 5.3 ABS Warning or No Communication - Identify and Test Before Module Work
records.description: Some 1998-2001 C5 A6 configurations use Bosch 5.3 brake electronics, but Audi documents several ABS/EDL, ASR, and ESP versions with engine- and transmission-specific coding. An ABS lamp, red brake warning, wheel-speed fault, or failure to communicate with address 03 does not by itself prove an internal control-module fault. Power, ground, connector, CAN communication, wheel-speed inputs, hydraulic/electrical tests, module identity, and coding must be checked. records.title: C5 A6 2.8L Rear-Engine Coolant Leak - Locate the Connection First
records.description: Audi repair literature for the C5 2.8L AHA engine identifies a rear coolant pipe and multiple sealed cooling-system connections. Owner reports on 2.8L AHA/ATQ cars also show why a leak at the rear of the engine cannot be assigned to one O-ring from symptoms alone: coolant can escape from a rear pipe connection, a heater-hose connector, the coolant-temperature-sensor connection, or another nearby joint and then run toward the transmission. The previous card mixed the different 2.7T layout into the 2.8L record, extended the claim through 2005, and prescribed four identical N90560701 seals without sufficient fitment evidence. This corrected record is limited to the 1998-2001 C5 A6 2.8L AHA/ATQ application and treats the visible leak location as a diagnosis, not a universal part order.
records.solution: With the engine cold, clean and dry the rear cooling-system connections and pressure-test the system using the Audi repair procedure. Trace fresh coolant to the exact joint before disassembly; specifically distinguish the rear coolant-pipe connections from the heater hoses/connectors and coolant-temperature-sensor seal. Replace only the pipe, hose, connector, or seal that is proven to leak, and renew any seals or gaskets the repair manual marks for replacement. Select every seal by VIN, engine code, and exact diagram position in the current Audi catalog. Refill with the correct Audi-compatible coolant and bleed and re-pressure-test the system. Do not order N90560701 from this card: the audit did not establish it as the correct universal seal or quantity for the 2.8L AHA/ATQ layout. Stop driving if the coolant warning or temperature rises, because continued coolant loss can cause overheating.

records.title: C5 Sunroof and Fresh-Air Plenum Drain Water Ingress
records.description: The federal Dewey settlement record identifies 1998-2005 Audi A6 C5 vehicles with the 4B platform code, including allroad, S, and RS versions, among vehicles alleged to be susceptible to passenger-compartment water ingress through sunroof drains or the fresh-air plenum. This page-level record is conservatively scoped to 1998-2004 A6 model years so it is not shown as a universal condition on a 2005 C6 sedan; a 2005 allroad owner should confirm the 4B platform by VIN. Audi A6 C5 repair literature shows separate front and rear sunroof drain hoses and a cable-based cleaning procedure. Wet footwells or headliner do not prove that a drain hose itself needs replacement: debris, a restricted outlet, a disconnected or damaged hose, and the fresh-air plenum are different paths that must be checked separately. Water left under the carpet can damage electrical modules and wiring.
records.solution: Confirm the 4B platform/VIN and trace the leak before buying parts. Test each sunroof drain separately with a modest amount of water, then clean a blocked hose with the proper sunroof-drain snake or the flexible cable method described in the repair manual. Inspect each hose connection and outlet as well as the fresh-air plenum; replace a hose only when it is found disconnected, kinked, split, or otherwise damaged. The hose part number depends on body style, position, and VIN, so it must be selected from Audi's catalog after diagnosis. Remove and dry wet carpet and padding promptly and inspect any affected electrical modules or connectors. The previously listed 4A9877233 hose was not verified for this C5 application and is not a safe universal repair.

Damp or stained headliner or pillar trim
Musty odor or persistent interior-window fogging
Electrical faults after water accumulates beneath the carpet

records.title: 2019-2021 A6 3.0L Misfire Codes - Check ECM Software Before Mechanical Cleaning
records.description: For a 2019-2021 Audi A6 equipped with the 3.0L TFSI engine, the malfunction indicator lamp may illuminate with P0300 and one or more cylinder-specific P0301-P0306 codes. Audi's service information identifies an applicable ECM software-calibration condition and publishes model-year-specific software levels. Misfire codes alone do not prove intake-valve carbon buildup, and the previous card incorrectly grouped 2011-2023 A6 models, multiple unrelated engine generations, a fixed walnut-blasting interval, fuel additives, universal catch cans, and generic shopping searches into one diagnosis. This corrected record covers only the Audi-documented software condition; carbon cleaning or parts replacement requires separate physical diagnosis if the misfire remains after the software level and other common causes are checked.
records.solution: Record every stored DTC and freeze-frame before clearing faults. records.title: Electrical Issues (Window Regulators, Door Locks, MMI)
records.description: The Audi A6 is prone to various electrical gremlins across all generations, including window regulator failures, door lock actuator failures, MMI/infotainment glitches, and battery drain issues. Window regulators fail due to weak plastic clips in the mechanism, causing windows to drop into the door or move slowly. Door lock actuators wear out, causing doors to unlock randomly, fail to lock, or make grinding noises. MMI (Multi Media Interface) infotainment systems freeze, reboot randomly, or display "SAFE" mode. Battery drain issues (parasitic draw) are common, leaving the car dead after sitting for a few days. Many electrical issues are caused by aging control modules, corroded connectors, or software bugs. While frustrating, most electrical issues are not safety-critical and can be addressed individually as they arise.
records.solution: Window regulator replacement: $300-$600 per window (DIY $150-$250 with aftermarket kit). Order regulator with metal clips, not plastic. Door lock actuator: $200-$400 per door at dealer, DIY $50-$100 per actuator (1-hour job). MMI/infotainment glitches: Perform hard reset (hold power + volume up for 10 seconds). If that fails, Audi dealer can update software or replace MMI unit ($1,000-$2,500). Battery drain: Have dealer perform parasitic draw test to identify faulty module. Common culprits: trunk electronics, MMI, comfort control module. Address issues as they arise—most are minor annoyances, not showstoppers.
symptoms: Window drops into door or won't roll up/down
Door locks fail to lock or unlock (one or more doors)
Grinding or clicking noise from door when locking
MMI screen freezes, reboots, or shows "SAFE" mode
Battery dies after car sits for 2-3 days
Warning lights for systems that work fine (phantom codes)
Backup camera, parking sensors, or adaptive cruise intermittent

records.title: Front Suspension Multi-Link Control Arm and Tie-Rod Wear Causing Clunks and Tire Wear
records.description: The C5 A6 uses a multi-link aluminum front suspension with multiple upper and lower control arms whose ball joints and bushings commonly wear out, especially on rough roads or higher-mileage cars. Owners frequently report front-end clunking over bumps, wandering steering, vibration, and uneven inner-edge tire wear. This is one of the most commonly discussed C5 chassis wear items across owner forums and repair databases.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually involves checking for play in the upper and lower control arm ball joints, torn bushings, and worn tie-rod ends with the suspension loaded. The durable repair is replacement of the failed arms, and many owners replace the full front control-arm kit at once followed by a four-wheel alignment. Tie rods and sway-bar links are often inspected or replaced at the same time.

records.title: Gateway Control Module Liquid-Ingress Recall 90V2 (22V-861)
records.description: Certain 2019-2022 Audi A6 Sedan and 2020-2022 A6 allroad vehicles are included in safety recall 22V-861, Audi campaign 90V2.
